reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: 01e property (outputs/01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json, lines 678-694): 'Blobs from local EL that skip KZG verification must still produce valid data columns.' Code reading verified: For Fulu blocks (message_router.nim:155-193), dataColumnsOpt is passed directly from beacon_validators.nim:587-589, which calls assemble_data_column_sidecars with blobs from engineBlock.blobsBundle (Engine API, no KZG validation). The blobs are NOT validated before calling computeCells (peerdas_helpers.nim:325). However, this is a SEMI-TRUSTED boundary issue (Engine API, JWT-authenticated, co-located EL). Exploitation requires a compromised or buggy local EL. Per Step C2, this is a code-intrinsic deviation where the construction logic (data column assembly) relies on semi-trusted input rather than external attacker control. The spec requires valid columns, but an attacker cannot directly trigger this without first compromising the local EL. Attacker control: none (requires compromised EL first). Path type: semi-trusted. Severity reduced from High to Low due to semi-trusted boundary classification per BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json trust_assumptions.engine_api.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: EIP-7594 PeerDAS requires valid data columns from blobs; Engine API is semi-trusted boundary
